relationships.description: The multi-step journey reads from or writes to a persistent collection as it progresses, for example saving a draft order at an intermediate step or committing the final record when the last step completes.
relationships.evidence: A step handler or flow completion callback registered for the flow calls a repository or API endpoint that queries or inserts into the named table, document collection or bucket.

relationships.description: The journey reads or assembles instances of a structured domain record as the user moves through its steps, such as building up a CheckoutOrder or OnboardingProfile object that is submitted at the end.
relationships.evidence: The flow's state store or completion handler is typed against the schema's interface, DTO or model class and populates or validates its properties across the steps.

relationships.description: The journey opens and works with a specific page, screen or modal as one of the display surfaces the user passes through while completing the process.
relationships.evidence: The flow definition or wizard controller references the view component, either through a step's route target or by opening the modal directly, during the flow.

relationships.description: The journey groups the client-side state items it carries across its steps, such as a cart ID or selected plan, which each step writes or reads before the flow finishes.
relationships.evidence: The flow configuration lists the context variables with their schema, scope and storage mechanism, or the flow's state slice declares those keys in sessionStorage, localStorage, memory or the query string.

relationships.description: The journey collects its ordered steps into one grouping, with each step contributing one route and a sequence index to the overall process.
relationships.evidence: The flow definition's steps array lists the FlowStep entries with their order, route and skippable settings.

relationships.description: The journey owns its ordered steps outright, so each step's sequence position, skippability and wait behaviour only exist as part of this flow and disappear if the flow is removed.
relationships.evidence: The FlowStep entries are declared inline in the flow's definition object or wizard config and have no separate registration outside that flow.

relationships.description: Progress through the journey passes along a particular permitted route change, such as the move from the shipping route to the payment route, when the user advances between steps.
relationships.evidence: The flow's next and previous handlers call the router to perform a route change that matches a transition declared between the source and destination routes in the router configuration.

relationships.description: The client-side journey is the user-facing execution of an ordered application workflow, with its steps carrying out the stages of that process, such as a checkout saga or account-provisioning orchestration.
relationships.evidence: The flow's step transitions and completion handler invoke, in order, the service methods or workflow endpoints that make up the documented application process.

relationships.description: The journey is the digital means by which a user carries out a business process end to end, such as placing an order or enrolling as a customer, mapping its steps onto the process's activities.
relationships.evidence: Process documentation or a BPMN model maps each business activity to a step of the flow, and the flow's completion produces the process's defined result.

relationships.description: Delivering the journey makes concrete a stakeholder end state, such as frictionless purchasing or faster customer onboarding.
relationships.evidence: The product brief, epic or architecture decision record cites the goal as the reason the flow was introduced, and the flow's analytics are tied to that goal.

relationships.description: The journey is the concrete, route-based implementation in the client of a user workflow described from the persona's point of view, turning its user-facing steps into screens visited in order.
relationships.evidence: Product specs or story tickets link the user workflow to the flow, and each WorkflowStep corresponds to one or more FlowSteps in the flow definition.

relationships.description: The journey depends on a router guard to stop users entering or advancing through its steps out of order or without the required preconditions, such as reaching payment before a shipping address is captured.
relationships.evidence: The flow definition or its routes register the guard in a beforeEnter, canActivate or per-flow guards list, and the guard checks flow state before allowing navigation.

relationships.description: The journey meets a stated, verifiable need, such as 'users must be able to complete checkout in at most four steps', through its step order and behaviour.
relationships.evidence: The requirement's acceptance criteria reference the flow, and end-to-end tests that drive the flow through its steps are traced to the requirement ID.

relationships.description: The journey's step ordering and gating enforce the workflow-level duty and purpose rules of the security model, for example forcing an approval step to be performed by someone other than the requester.
relationships.evidence: Guards or step preconditions in the flow check the separation-of-duty, binding-of-duty or need-to-know rules defined in the security model, and security review documents trace those constraints to the flow.

relationships.description: The journey is the channel through which customers consume an externally visible business service, such as Order Delivery or Claims Handling, by completing it in the client.
relationships.evidence: The service catalogue or channel documentation lists the flow as the digital entry point for the business service, and the flow's final step submits the request to that service.

relationships.description: Starting, completing or abandoning the journey emits a named application event, such as CheckoutCompleted or OnboardingStarted, that other application behaviour reacts to.
relationships.evidence: The flow's start, completion or abandon handler dispatches or publishes the event by name to an event bus, store action or analytics/message topic.

relationships.description: Completing the journey initiates a downstream business process, such as order fulfilment or application review, that people in the organisation then carry out.
relationships.evidence: The flow's final submission creates a work item, case or order record that the business process documentation names as its start trigger.

relationships.description: The journey depends on a platform software product, such as the SPA router library's runtime, the browser storage engine or a cache server that holds flow state, to run and persist its progress.
relationships.evidence: The flow's implementation imports or configures the platform product, for example a router or state-persistence package declared in package.json or a Redis session store named in deployment config.

notes: aggregates and composes FlowStep conflict; FlowStep exists only within a flow, so composes is correct and aggregates should be dropped. Realizing a Goal is questionable; supports fits better. accesses View overlaps the step-to-route-to-view chain. flows-to NavigationTransition is odd, since a flow traverses or references transitions. uses SystemSoftware is weakly meaningful for a client-side flow.
